comment: Canonical Hound-Up help content. A byte-for-byte copy of this file also lives at houndup-web/help-content.json — if you edit one, edit both. Written in plain, short-sentence UK English on purpose (aiming for an easy reading level), for both the in-app Help Centre and houndup-web/help.html.

articles.title: What is Hound-Up?
body: Hound-Up is an app for dog walkers. It helps you keep track of your clients, their dogs, your walks and sits, and your invoices.
It works fully on your phone, with no internet needed. Your data backs up automatically via iCloud, so it's safe even if you never sign in — more on that below.

articles.title: Do I need to sign in?
body: No. Hound-Up works fully without signing in. You can add clients, log walks, and send invoices straight away — your data backs up automatically via iCloud either way.
Signing in is only needed for Hound-Up Pro's extra automation (Autopilot) — things like nudges and booking alerts happening even with the app closed. See "Free vs Hound-Up Pro" for the full list.

articles.title: Where does the weather come from?
body: The weather shown at the top of Today is based on the postcode saved in Business Details, not your phone's live location.
If it looks wrong, check that postcode is correct in Settings → Business Details.

articles.title: Adding your first client
body: Tap the + button on the Today tab, or go to the Dogs tab and tap "New dog".
You'll be asked for the dog's name and the owner's name and phone number. That's all you need to get started — you can fill in the rest of their details later.

articles.title: Adding a new client
body: Go to the Dogs tab and tap "New dog". Type the dog's name and the owner's details.
You can add more information later, like the owner's address, emergency contact, and any notes — just open the client's page and tap Edit.

articles.title: Adding a dog to an existing client
body: Open the client's page and tap "Add a dog". If they've already got one dog on file, this adds another one for the same owner — you won't need to type the owner's details again.

articles.title: Finding a client's address
body: When you're typing a client's address, start typing and a list of matching addresses will pop up. Tap the right one and it fills in the street, town and postcode for you.
Can't find it? Tap "Enter manually" underneath the search box and type the address in yourself.

articles.title: Adding a dog's vet
body: On a dog's page, tap Edit and use the "Search for a vet practice" box. If it finds the practice, it fills in the name and address for you.
If it can't find it, tap "Enter manually" and type the vet's name and address yourself.

articles.title: Editing a client or dog
body: Open the client or dog's page and tap Edit in the top corner. Change whatever you need, then tap Save.

articles.title: Logging a walk
body: Tap the + on Today and choose "Log a past walk". Pick the dog, the date, and how long the walk was. Hound-Up works out what to charge automatically, using your rates.
You can add a note or a photo too, if you like.

articles.title: Recording a walk live
body: Tap the + on Today and choose "Start a walk". Hound-Up tracks your route using GPS while you walk, and you tap "Stop & save" when you're done.
This needs Hound-Up to know your location while you're recording — you'll be asked to allow this the first time.

articles.title: Booking a one-off walk
body: Tap a day on the Calendar tab, or use the + button, and choose "Book a walk". Pick the dog (or add a new one), then the date and time.
This is for a single walk. If it's a regular booking, set up a schedule instead — see "Setting up a regular schedule".

articles.title: Setting up a regular schedule
body: Open a dog's page, go to the Schedule tab, and tap "Add a schedule". Pick the day of the week, the time, and how long the walk is.
Hound-Up creates each week's walk automatically, so you don't need to book it every time.

articles.title: Logging or booking a sit
body: Use the + button and choose "Log a sit" or "Book a sit" from the Calendar tab. Sits can be a few hours or several days — Hound-Up bills by the night for anything longer than a day.

articles.title: How invoicing works
body: Every walk and sit you log gets added to that client's running total, on the Ledger tab. When you're ready, you turn that total into an invoice and send it.
You don't have to invoice after every single walk — most walkers send one invoice a month for everything a client owes.

articles.title: Sending an invoice
body: Go to the Ledger tab, open a client's outstanding balance, and tap Send. You can send it by email or WhatsApp, straight from your phone's own Mail or WhatsApp app.

articles.title: Getting paid by card or Apple Pay
body: Hound-Up can add a "Pay now" link to your invoices, so clients can pay you by card or Apple Pay. Set this up in Settings > Payment Details by connecting your own Stripe account.
The money goes straight into your own Stripe account — Hound-Up never touches it or takes a cut.

articles.title: Marking an invoice as paid
body: Open the invoice and tap "Mark as paid". If you're signed in to Hound-Up Pro and a client pays through your Stripe "Pay now" link, this happens automatically instead — see "Free vs Hound-Up Pro".

articles.title: Nudging a late payment
body: On the Ledger tab, overdue invoices show a "Nudge" button — this sends a polite reminder. With Hound-Up Pro, this can also happen by itself, without you needing to open the app.

articles.title: Exporting your income for tax
body: Go to the Ledger tab and tap the export icon at the top. Choose a tax year (or your own date range) and Hound-Up creates a spreadsheet of everything you've earned, ready for your tax return or your accountant.

articles.title: What is the booking requests page?
body: It's a web page you can share with clients (or put on your own website) so they can ask you for a walk without phoning or texting you first.
Turn it on in Settings > Booking Requests. You'll get a link to share.

articles.title: Turning on your availability calendar
body: This shows clients which times you're actually free, right on your booking page, so they can just tap a time instead of guessing. Turn it on in Settings > Booking Requests.
It's just a helpful guide for clients — it doesn't stop two people picking the same time by accident, so you'll still want to check and confirm any request yourself.

articles.title: Accepting or declining a request
body: New requests show up as a notification in the app — tap it to see the details. If the person's already one of your clients, Hound-Up recognises them automatically and won't create a duplicate.
Tap Accept to book it in, or Decline if it doesn't work for you.

articles.title: What is Autopilot?
body: Autopilot is the part of Hound-Up Pro that keeps things running even with the app closed — nudging late payers, keeping your booking page and calendar feed live, and telling you straight away about a new request or a payment. You turn it on by signing in with Apple.
It's not a backup feature — your data already backs up automatically via iCloud whether or not you ever turn this on. See "Free vs Hound-Up Pro" for exactly what Autopilot adds.

articles.title: Free vs Hound-Up Pro
body: Hound-Up is free to use, with no limits on clients, dogs, walks or invoices, and backs up automatically via iCloud either way. Hound-Up Pro is £9.99 a month and adds Autopilot — automation that keeps running even with the app closed. Here's exactly what's different.

articles.title: How do I upgrade to Hound-Up Pro?
body: Go to Settings > Autopilot and tap Upgrade. You'll see the price and what's included, then Apple's own payment screen. Once you've paid, you'll be asked to sign in with Apple to finish setting it up.

articles.title: Managing or cancelling your subscription
body: Go to Settings > Autopilot and tap "Manage subscription" — this opens Apple's own subscription screen, where you can cancel or change it any time.

If you cancel, you keep everything until the end of the period you've already paid for. After that, Hound-Up goes back to working exactly like the free version — nothing is deleted, and your data keeps backing up via iCloud exactly as before.

articles.title: Automatic backup via iCloud
body: Hound-Up backs up your clients, dogs, walks, sits, invoices and ledger automatically, using your own iCloud account. There's nothing to turn on, and no account with Hound-Up needed — it just works, the same way iCloud backs up your Photos.

This needs iCloud to be switched on for Hound-Up on your iPhone, which it is by default. If you've turned iCloud off for apps generally, check Settings (the iPhone's own Settings app, not Hound-Up's) → your name → iCloud → See All, and make sure Hound-Up is on there.

One thing this doesn't cover: your own business profile (name, address, rates, logo, bank details) stays only on this device unless you also sign in to Hound-Up Pro's Autopilot — see "What is Autopilot?" for why.

articles.title: Backing up your data yourself
body: Go to Settings > Data and tap "Export all data". This saves everything — clients, dogs, walks, invoices, even photos — as one file you can save anywhere: Files, email, Google Drive, wherever you like.

This is completely free and doesn't need you to sign in. Your data already backs up automatically via iCloud (see "Automatic backup via iCloud"), but this is a good extra copy to keep somewhere outside of Apple's own ecosystem too.

articles.title: Restoring from a backup
body: Go to Settings > Data and tap "Restore from backup". Choose the file you saved earlier. Hound-Up shows you what's in it before doing anything, so you can check it's the right one.
Restoring replaces everything currently on your phone with what's in the backup — so make sure that's what you want first.

articles.title: Erasing all your data
body: Go to Settings > Data and tap "Erase all data". This can't be undone, so Hound-Up will ask you to confirm first — it clears your iCloud backup too, since that's just a copy of what's on your phone.
If you're signed in to Hound-Up Pro, this doesn't automatically delete your Autopilot data — use Settings → Autopilot → "Delete cloud data" for that separately.

articles.title: Turning on notifications
body: Go to Settings > Notifications to turn on things like a daily digest or invoicing reminders. The first time you turn one on, Hound-Up will ask you to confirm before the phone's own permission prompt appears.

articles.title: What you get told about, and how
body: Hound-Up tells you about things in three ways: a bell icon in the app, a notification that pops up on your phone (even with the app shut), and sometimes an email. Not everything uses all three — here's how it works.
Getting a new booking request and getting paid are the two big ones. Both always show up in the bell icon. With Hound-Up Pro, both also pop up on your phone straight away.
Getting paid also always sends you an email — free or Pro. Money matters, so we tell you either way, even if the pop-up notification is a Pro-only extra.

Quieter jobs running in the background — like an automatic payment reminder or visit summary going out — only show up in the bell icon. They don't pop up on your phone. If several of these happened at once, a pop-up for every single one would just be annoying, so the bell icon is where they live instead.

articles.title: Daily digest
body: A single notification each morning summing up what's on today — how many walks, and anything that needs your attention. Turn it on in Settings > Notifications.

articles.title: Invoicing reminders
body: A reminder on the day of the month you choose, nudging you to send out invoices for everything logged that month. Turn it on and set the day in Settings > Notifications.
